voyage.name: Vieux Port
voyage.content: Watching fishermen selling their stock by auction is a must. Arriving into Marseille in the Vieux-Port on a summer evening is something you will never forget. You can watch this show by going to Frioul islands or Chateau d'If and going back late in the afternoon. There is also a nice view of the harbour from the Palais du Pharo (Pharo Palace). The famous Canebière avenue goes straight down the harbour. However the Ca

voyage.name: Basilique Notre Dame de la Garde
voyage.content: The big church which overlooks the city. Old fishermen used to have their boats blessed in this church. You can still see many boat models hanging around in the church. From there it is one of the nicest view of the city. You can use the tourist train from the Vieux Port to reach the church - you can get off the train, look around and board a later train back to the port.

voyage.name: L'Hotel de Ville
voyage.content: Marseille City Hall

voyage.name: Le Panier
voyage.content: Le Panier (which means basket in French) is the historical centre of the city. This district is characterized by many narrow and steep streets. The tourist office organises a guided tour in English of the Old town every Saturday at 14:00. You can begin your tour from the Vieux-Port and finish at the Mucem or vice versa. A recommended trail of this district is also proposed by the tourist office.

voyage.name: Marseille Cathedral
voyage.alt: Cathédrale Sainte-Marie-Majeure de Marseille or Cathédrale de la Major
voyage.content: A Byzantine-Roman cathedral at the western side of Le Panier quarter.

voyage.name: La Vieille Charité
voyage.content: is a wonderful old monument, a former charitable housing for poor, now hosting museums and exhibitions.

voyage.name: Place Castellane
voyage.content: With a grand fountain/column/sculpture in the center, with excellent cinemas and cafés surrounding. There is another place called La Castellane: it is a poor suburb of Marseille where famous footballer Zinedine Zidane was born.

voyage.name: Cours Julien
voyage.content: A hangout area with bookstores, cafés, fountains, and a playground for the small ones. It is a trendy area of Marseille.

voyage.name: Place Jean Jaurès
voyage.content: La Plaine is the local name for Place Jean Jaurès close to Cours Julien. Every Thursday and Saturday morning the Plaine market is the place to shop. If you are there early enough you can make very good deals, even if what you'll find there is sometimes "tombé du camion" (fallen off the truck) as one says in Marseille.

voyage.name: Noailles quarter
voyage.content: Lined with Arabic and Indo-Chinese shops some of the streets could be part of a bazzaar in Algeria. A fascinating area.

voyage.name: Palais Longchamp
voyage.content: It houses the city's Musée des Beaux-Arts and Natural History Museum. The surrounding park (the Parc Longchamp) is listed by the French Ministry of Culture as one of the Notable Gardens of France. The Boulevard Longchamp connects it with the city centre.

voyage.name: Fort Saint-Jean
voyage.content: Fort Saint-Jean is a fortification at the North-Western end of the Old Port, built in 1660 by Louis XIV. The fort also hosts the Museum "Musée des Civilisations de l'Europe et de la Méditerranée", but the fortification itself is accessible to the public free of cost, and worth a visit. You can walk through the old fortifications, stroll through a small park, enjoy the view on the Old Port or on the sea, or walk over

voyage.name: Vallon des Auffes
voyage.content: Small and out of time traditional fishing port, just near the city centre.

voyage.name: Parc Borély
voyage.content: A large and great park containing Château Borély, 300 meters from the sea. After a siesta in the park go have a drink at Escale Borely (a place with numerous restaurants and bars on the beach) to see the sunset.

voyage.name: Musée des Civilisations de l'Europe et de la Méditerranée
voyage.content: The first French national museum outside of Paris. It has large permanent and temporary exhibitions. Its architecture mixes a very contemporary structure (a dark box) with an old castle, with footbridges linking the two parts of the museum.

voyage.name: Musée des beaux-arts de Marseille
voyage.content: The painting collection includes works of the French, Italian, Spanish and Northern (Flanders and Holland) schools.

voyage.name: Natural History Museum
voyage.address: Palais Longchamp (aile droite), Boulevard Jardin Zoologique

voyage.name: Musée Cantini
voyage.content: Museum focusing on modern art from the late 19th century until the mid-late 20th century.

voyage.name: Museum of Contemporary Art [MAC]
voyage.content: Later works from the Cantini collection. Situated in southern suburbs but easily reached by Metro then bus. Now reopened after a major refurbishment.

voyage.name: FRAC Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur
voyage.content: Contemporary art in a building designed by architect Kengo Kuma. Part of a national network .

voyage.name: Musée des Docks Romains
voyage.content: Built to preserve the archeological finds at the former warehouses of the old harbour from Phoenician and Roman times. (closed summer 23 check before going)

voyage.name: Archaeological Museum
voyage.address: Centre de la Vieille Charité, 2 Rue de la Charité
voyage.content: Displays of Egyptian antiquities and classical antiquities.

voyage.name: Marseille History Museum (MHM)
voyage.price: Permanent collections: free; Exhibitions circa €6, reduced €3
voyage.content: Discover 26 centuries of history in archaeology, fine arts, everyday objects & architecture. There is a mobile app.

voyage.name: Deportation Memorial
voyage.content: Memorial & museum relating to repression & persecution during World War II. Run by the Marseille History Museum (MHM).

voyage.name: Museum of the Decorative Arts, Fashion and Ceramics
voyage.alt: Musée des Arts décoratifs, de la Faïence et de la Mode
voyage.content: Château Borély and its grounds are pretty impressive before you start with the museum. Often the exhibits are scattered amongst the furniture in the house.

voyage.name: Motorcycle Museum
voyage.price: Permanent collection: free, exhibitions eur6-12 also free for -18 & EU students 18-26
voyage.address: 18 rue Jean Marsac Quartier du Merlan
voyage.content: Museum in a former flour mill featuring motorcycles from 1885 to the present day. Four levels of bikes. It may look closed but you need to press the button by the gate to gain admission.

voyage.name: Mazargues War Cemetery
voyage.content: A war cemetery dedicated to World War I and World War II martyrs from the Allies, especially the Indian and Chinese gunners and runners. A very serene place, it is the perfect place to spend sometime thinking about the people who laid down their lives to give us the freedom we enjoy today.

voyage.name: Unité d'Habitation
voyage.content: Designed by Le Corbusier, and one of 17 of his buildings to be listed as a World Heritage Site. The building is called "la maison du fada" (the house of the foolish) by locals. The building contains a shopping street, a church, a children's school and housing. You can access the roof and enjoy the breathtaking view of Marseille between hills and sea (10:00-18:00). There is a bar/restaurant/hotel on the 3rd floor too.

voyage.name: Artplexe
voyage.content: New multi-screen cinema showing some films in VO combined with exhibition spaces and restaurant.

voyage.name: Cinéma l'Alhambra
voyage.content: Art House Cinema with original 1930s facade out of the city centre. Shows some films in VO (the original language)

voyage.name: City of Music
voyage.content: Music school & concert halls Diverse musical types

voyage.name: CEPAC Silo
voyage.content: Concert venue/theatre in a former grain silo. The performance space is reconfigurable according to the type of show performed. Total capacity 2,050 seats.

voyage.name: Café Cantine
voyage.content: This little place has the best food made fresh onsite! Very kind and friendly staff. Fast service, fresh and good products. Very warm welcome and very good homemade meal.

voyage.name: Sampolo
voyage.content: Sampolo is a nice family place. The dishes and desserts are very tasty and homemade. Great place and great atmosphere in the evening.

voyage.name: Brasserie Le Saint Victor
voyage.content: A very friendly neighborhood brasserie with good traditional dishes and caring, fast and efficient staff. The catering is excellent with a wide variety of daily specials.

voyage.name: Moon Burger
voyage.content: The quality is exceptional, the products are fresh, the bread is homemade, the meat is succulent. The homemade sauces are top of the line. Also the staff is very warm and attentive.

voyage.name: Santa Pizza
voyage.content: Very good pizza and pasta. Hearty toppings, thin crust, tasty ingredients.

voyage.name: Perle d'Asie
voyage.content: A cuisine that makes us rediscover Asian flavors. There is a possibility of having vegetarian spring rolls.

voyage.name: five pizza original
voyage.content: Interesting concept, which is very simple: You create your pizza by choosing all the toppings of your pizza with a lot of choice on an electronic terminal.

voyage.name: Restaurant Le Palmier
voyage.content: A very good Tunisian restaurant with a good welcome and a good meal.

voyage.name: Chez Tri
voyage.content: An extraordinary and very pleasant Vietnamese restaurant! Fresh and especially homemade products.

voyage.name: Le Par Azar - Restaurant Libanais
voyage.content: Small Lebanese restaurant. The food is very good, homemade and very fresh. The small terrace is pleasant even if it is on the side of the road.

voyage.name: New School Tacos
voyage.content: Super welcoming and the quality of the tacos is exceptionally good.

voyage.name: L'heure de Marseille
voyage.content: Very good Indian and Pakanian dishes and fast food. Quiet street with terrace. Best Naan Poulet.

voyage.name: Bodrum City Kebab
voyage.content: Clean and comfortable establishment, air-conditioned room. Very pleasant staff. Wide variety of choice and very tasty for dishes.

voyage.name: Sur le Pouce
voyage.content: Very tasty, copious and affordable Tunisian restaurant.

voyage.name: Café l'Écomotive
voyage.content: Excellent veggie café

voyage.name: Flower burger
voyage.content: Multi coloured buns and no meat.

voyage.name: V&V House
voyage.content: Fast food place with wide choice of vegan options including Poke bowls.

voyage.name: L'Usyne
voyage.content: Small Vietnamese restaurant & tea house. Good choice of veggie dishes.

voyage.name: Four des Navettes
voyage.content: This bakery is famous for its "Navette" dry biscuit which recipe has been kept secret for almost a century. This is one of Marseille's culinary specialities. Not to miss, through you can get it in other bakeries in Marseille, too.

voyage.name: La Boite à Sardine
voyage.content: Despite its name, there is no canned fish in the menu there. A member of Gourméditerrannée association.

voyage.name: Le Cercle Rouge
voyage.content: This unusual restaurant does excellent Corsican tapas such as figatelli sausage, stuffed artichokes, panchetta in honey and red mullet in tomato sauce. Worth booking to get a spot on the lovely terrace.

voyage.name: La Riviera
voyage.content: Good fish restaurant where you can try "Soupe de poisson à la rouille" and other Marseille's sea food. Sea view.

voyage.name: Mariposas
voyage.content: Popular and highly regarded Vegan restaurant.

voyage.name: Le Glacier du Roi
voyage.content: Perhaps the best ice cream establishment in the city. Yet another member of Gourméditerrannée association.

voyage.name: Chez Michel
voyage.content: For bouillabaisse and other sea food.

voyage.name: Chez Fonfon
voyage.content: Seafood (again bouillabaisse), nice views.

voyage.name: L'Epuisette
voyage.content: Its amazing location in the very picturesque Vallon des Auffes harbour is an undeniable plus. Seafood specialities and affordable bouillabaisse.

voyage.name: La Table du Fort
voyage.content: A gastronomical restaurant consistently ranked among the city's best, specialized in seafood and fish dishes.

voyage.name: Le Petit Nice Passédat
voyage.content: A 3-star Michelin restaurant on an idyllic location by the sea, facing the islands, held by local celebrity chef Gérald Passédat. It ranks among Southern France's very best restaurants and serves the best bouillabaisse in town at a cost.

voyage.name: 1860 Le Palais
voyage.content: Very good classic French cuisine, made from quality products, in the historic building of the Chamber of Commerce. One of the best places near the old port.

voyage.name: Red Lion cours Julian
voyage.content: Small pub

voyage.name: Red Lion
voyage.content: English pub at La Pointe Rouge, southern Marseille, next to the beach.

voyage.name: Beer District Marseille
voyage.content: Beer Hall

voyage.name: Les BerThoM Marseille
voyage.content: Modern craft beer bar.

voyage.name: La Cane bière
voyage.content: Enormous selection for such a small place. Confusingly not on the Canebière.

voyage.name: La Brasserie Communale
voyage.content: Microbrewery serving locally brewed beers

voyage.name: Bière Academy
voyage.content: Craft beer bar a few streets away from the old port.

voyage.name: Polikarpov
voyage.content: Lively and good value late bar with outside terrace. Does a wide range of cocktails and one of the cheaper places for beer.

voyage.name: Le Marengo
voyage.content: In "Le Panier", a nice terrace with a nice atmosphere

voyage.name: Bar des 13 Coins
voyage.content: Next to the Old Port, small bar with terrace which offers a huge number of cocktails for €5.

voyage.name: Le Trolleybus
voyage.content: This three room cave-like club, is a great place to go if you like to listen to different types of music. One room or cave, plays hit music, another room plays underground techno and house music (room led by La Dame Noir records), and the last room plays jazzy and 1950-60s music. The drink prices range from €5 for a mixed drink or well beer to €10 for more quality alcohol.

voyage.name: Le Cosy Bar
voyage.content: Le Cosy Bar is a club aimed at the younger demographic. This is a multi-roomed club, plays top music in techno, dub step, hip hop, and reggae til 06:00. Le Cosy Bar is known for their extravagant theme nights such as Moscow Beach, where everyone's attire is mixed between winter wear and beach clothes, and Soiree Pyjamas, where everyone dressing in pajamas. The drink prices are €5-10, like most of the other night club

voyage.name: Le Baby
voyage.content: The best electronic music club in Marseille. €5 in advance or €10 with a drink.

voyage.name: Le Palais de la Major
voyage.content: Restaurant and club under the Major cathedral, the place hosts live bands from Corsica playing French and international hits. The place is luxurious and beautiful people fit in.

voyage.name: Hello Marseille Hostel
voyage.content: It's in a safe area in the very center of Marseille, the “Vieux Port”. They offer large shared rooms (with lockers) accommodating 6 people for the single price of €20. 24/7 reception & security. multilingual staff, no curfew; Online booking and reservation. Breakfast offered (French baguette, butter & marmalade, fruit, coffee); Linens included. Services: laundry, luggage storage, printer, free city bikes spot; free W

voyage.name: Hotel Lutetia
voyage.content: From €60. Between the St Charles Train Station and the old port +33 491 508 178. A renovated hostel with free internet, great atmosphere, and friendly staff.

voyage.name: Auberge de Jeunesse Marseille - Bois Luzy
voyage.hours: reception 09:00 - 10:00, 17:00 - 21:00. Closed from Late November to the start of March
voyage.content: The hostel is in a château north of the city centre, about 15 minutes walk from the Metro station. Beautiful views across the city.

voyage.name: Adagio Marseille Prado Plage
voyage.content: Completely renovated, the residence is in the heart of the Le Prado quarter, 100 metres from the beach, easy to get to via the Avenue du Prado or the Corniche. It lies in a quiet residential area close to a large number of restaurants and the Palais des Congrès. This site can accommodate people with reduced mobility (minor disabilities, elderly people) with an able-bodied escort and families with young children.

voyage.name: Hotel Kyriad Rabatau
voyage.content: Clean basic hotel. Room includes air-conditioner, bathroom and water boiler. Nearest metro station Sainte-Marguerite Dromel is situated 1.2 km from hotel to south.

voyage.name: Greet Hotel Marseille Centre Saint Charles
voyage.content: Newish Eco brand from Accor with a different look & feel inside. Friendly staff. Close to transport connections.

voyage.name: Hotel La résidence du Vieux Port Marseille
voyage.content: Completely renovated in 2010 in a 1950s style with a tribute to Charlotte Perriand and Le Corbusier. The hotel offers beautiful views of Marseille from its balconies and three suites on the top floor have terraces overlooking the Old Harbour and the Church. All the rooms are facing the port.

voyage.name: Best Western La Joliette
voyage.content: Clean, cosy hotel in a quiet location near Joliette metro/tram station. Good location for the port and Le Panier.

voyage.name: Novotel Marseille Vieux Port
voyage.content: A four-star resort near the Pharo gardens overlooking the Vieux Port with impressive views. The place to stay for most public figures.

voyage.name: Le Petit Nice Passedat
voyage.content: One of the city's most upmarket hotels, this villa by the sea boasts the region's only Michelin 3-star restaurant.
